subject: general
question: If sqrt{x} = (80)/(sqrt{4900)}, then what is the value of x?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Simplify the denominator on the right side: √4900 = 70.

The equation becomes √x = 80 / 70 = 8 / 7.

Square both sides to find x: x = (8 / 7)² = 64 / 49.

**∴ The correct answer is 64/49.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: √x = 80 / √4900

Formula Used: (√a)² = a

⇒ √x = 80 / √(49 × 100)

⇒ √x = 80 / (7 × 10)

⇒ √x = 80 / 70

⇒ √x = 8 / 7

⇒ (√x)² = (8 / 7)²

⇒ x = 64 / 49

**∴ The correct answer is 64/49.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Square Root of Large Numbers

To find √4900, simplify it as √(49 × 100) = 7 × 10 = 70. For numbers ending in double zeros, the square root ends in a single zero.

Squaring Property

If √x = k, then x = k². Squaring both sides is the standard algebraic method to remove a square root and isolate the variable.
